headline: Graph models couple network topology with local features in biological prediction tasks
label: Graph Learning For Biological Networks
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply graph neural networks and hypergraph models to protein, gene regulatory, drug synergy, and single-cell problems.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit modeling of relational structure rather than flat feature tables. Several items separate and recombine relational views: GLH2Syn pairs global diffusion with structure-aware local learning on a heterogeneous hypergraph for drug synergy, and HV-MultiScaleGNN compares local, global, and combined graph views for host-virus protein interactions. scGPL jointly models global regulatory graph topology with pairwise TF-target interactions for GRN inference from scRNA-seq. ProtLink instead augments PPI topology with frozen ESM-2 sequence features and cross-species orthogroup edges, with HGT reaching AP 0.970 on human PPI. scAdaG2M transfers graph structure into an MLP via distillation to address over-smoothing in scRNA-seq clustering. The shared element is the decomposition of relational information into topological, auxiliary, and local-versus-global components rather than a single pooled graph.
